Split by conversation before learning vocabulary, preprocessing or model parameters. Keep every message/window from a conversation in one partition, deduplicate near-identical content, and freeze a grouped test set. If deployment predicts future conversations, add a chronological boundary as well. Rebuild validation rather than treating leaked results as a usable baseline. Fit any learned normalization, vocabulary and label weights on training only.

Inspect token-length distributions and hand-check long examples with the final label-bearing sentence. Replace blind head truncation with a documented strategy justified by available inference content: a larger supported context, head-and-tail retention, or overlapping windows with conversation-level aggregation. A tail-only shortcut needs its own validation and can miss evidence elsewhere. Keep source-to-token offsets through normalization; never use the known label to choose inference windows.

For masked mean pooling, sum only real-token representations and divide by the count of included tokens, excluding padding and any special tokens the representation policy excludes. Define an empty-input outcome and avoid division by zero. Aggregate and deduplicate overlapping windows before one prediction per supervision unit.

Compare a lexical baseline and corrected model using macro/per-class F1, support, confusion and length/language slices on grouped data. Tune thresholds on validation, then evaluate the frozen test once.
answers.verification: Proposed: assert disjoint conversation IDs, inspect token/offset fixtures, compare a sample alone versus padded in a batch, and test empty, Unicode and long examples. No training or evaluation was executed.

The artifact treats rows as examples and columns as mutually exclusive classes. Inputs are logits, not probabilities; applying softmax before this function would change the contract. Subtracting each row maximum keeps exponentials bounded, and computing loss from the logit gap avoids taking log of an underflowed target probability. Scaling the gap components by batch size before subtraction also avoids some avoidable intermediate overflow. A mathematically unrepresentable floating-point mean can still be infinite; finite inputs alone cannot guarantee representable loss at arbitrary magnitudes.

The returned loss is the batch mean. Each gradient row is (softmax minus the target one-hot vector) divided by the same batch size. Neither input is mutated. Ragged/empty batches, fewer than two classes, invalid labels, unsupported values and nonfinite logits raise ValueError.

For a proposed derivative check, use a small nonsymmetric double-precision fixture and central differences: perturb one logit by plus/minus epsilon and compare the resulting mean-loss difference divided by twice epsilon with the returned component. Restore the value after each perturbation and use identical labels/reduction. Also check uniform logits, correct-class dominance, extreme gaps, row-gradient sums near zero, and invariance to an ordinary shared row offset. No code was executed.
answers.verification: Proposed finite-difference, extreme-logit, mean-reduction, malformed-input and no-mutation checks; none were executed.

Keep OpenTelemetry as the instrumentation layer and the configured Azure exporter as its destination; inspect installed packages before choosing concrete APIs. Filter routine successful health-probe spans at instrumentation where supported, while retaining probe failure counts and availability metrics. Do not make health endpoints invisible to operations. Use parent-aware sampling and retain the error/slow-request information needed for diagnosis.

At enqueue, inject W3C trace context into bounded message metadata. At consume, extract it and create a consumer/process span in the extracted context, or use span links where batching/multiple producer contexts makes a single parent misleading. Scope and detach context per message so workers do not inherit the previous job. Track retries and processing failures without putting payload text in spans.

Record request duration histograms, request/failure counters, throughput and queue age using stable route/service/outcome dimensions. Derive p95 from the histogram and failure rate from matching counts and windows; avoid customer, request and trace IDs as metric labels. Redact customer text before export, using allowlisted event fields and trace correlation IDs.

Replace single-request paging with sustained user-impact/SLO conditions, such as multiwindow error-budget burn and a latency objective with traffic safeguards. Assign an owner, runbook and recovery condition. Bound exporter queues/timeouts so collector failures cannot exhaust memory or block requests.
answers.verification: Proposed: trace a synthetic queued job, check context isolation across two messages, inject failure/latency and verify alert trigger/recovery, inspect redaction, and simulate an unavailable exporter. No service or alert changes were executed.

The sorted samples are already in order. Baseline median is 8 ms; its mean is (32 + 80)/5 = 22.4 ms. Candidate median is 5 ms and mean is (20 + 120)/5 = 28 ms. With nearest-rank p95, rank = ceil(0.95 × 5) = 5, so p95 is 80 ms for baseline and 120 ms for candidate.

The candidate median decreases 37.5%, but mean increases 25% and observed p95 increases 50%. It is therefore a tradeoff with a tail regression in these samples, not evidence that the optimization meets an objective including tail latency. Five samples make this p95 the maximum and provide weak evidence about a stable population percentile.

Reinstate timeouts and errors as first-class outcomes; report their counts, rates, timeout deadlines and any latency censoring instead of silently discarding them. Separate cold-start and warm distributions, retaining their realistic traffic mix. Memory has not been measured, so the memory objective remains unevaluated.

Before promotion, verify equivalent results, then run repeated/interleaved matched trials under representative concurrency and cache hit/miss behavior. Record runtime, hardware, workload, throughput, resident/peak memory, allocations, tail distributions and failure rates. Define acceptance against both latency and memory budgets and retain raw outcomes.
answers.verification: Arithmetic above is derived directly from the supplied samples. Repeated load, cold-start, timeout and memory measurements are proposed and were not performed.

Make configuration location a documented contract. Resolve an explicit --config path as supplied, otherwise use a stable application/user configuration directory; use importlib.resources for package-owned defaults. Do not accidentally infer installed resources from the caller’s current directory or the source checkout. Preserve intentional user-relative path semantics where the interface documents them, and give a useful error for a missing explicit file.

Declare the required runtime dependency in pyproject.toml project dependencies with justified supported bounds. Check that it supports Python 3.11–3.14; separate optional features into extras only if their imports are genuinely conditional. Keep build-only requirements in the build-system declaration.

Declare the CLI in project.scripts, pointing to an importable packaged module/function, and include its code/default data in the distribution. A console wrapper is normally generated at installation from entry-point metadata; checking only for a physical wrapper inside the wheel is insufficient.

Produce an sdist, then build the wheel from that archive in isolation. Inspect the inventories, dependency metadata and entry_points.txt. Clean-install the resulting wheel into fresh environments for each of 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14, with the checkout excluded. Invoke --help and a representative command from unrelated directories, with explicit/default/missing config. Record unavailable interpreters rather than claiming compatibility.
answers.verification: Proposed distribution inventory, isolated wheel-from-sdist build and four-interpreter clean-install matrix. No builds, installations or commands were executed.

This candidate is not publication-ready: local tests, CI, tag, artifacts, website and registry do not establish one accepted release identity. Preserve their current states and prepare corrections without publishing, deleting or moving any tag. Record the exact tested local commit, CI commit/run URL, original/current tag targets, artifact hashes and metadata, website claims, and the version actually available on PyPI.

Choose one accepted immutable source revision and intended version. A CI pass for another commit is not transferable evidence; require the necessary checks on that accepted revision. Quarantine the existing artifact set from promotion until its provenance is resolved. Build each intended target once from the accepted tree, record hashes, and clean-install outside the checkout. For Python, also verify the wheel built from the produced sdist.

Prepare a website change that labels the candidate accurately and links only verified available downloads. Do not apply it in this preparation-only task. Avoid silently moving an existing public tag again; plan a new immutable candidate/version and preserve a documented history. If a registry version is already immutable, supersede it through its supported mechanism rather than replacing bytes.

The publication gate binds source, version, CI evidence, immutable tag, artifact hashes and destination plan. Obtain the destination-specific authorization, promote the same verified bytes, then verify registry/download availability before announcing release. Include recovery for partial publication.
answers.verification: Proposed release identity matrix, accepted-revision CI, artifact/install checks and destination readback. No publication, deletion, tag movement or website modification was performed.

The pointer has two hazards: Vec growth may relocate its allocation, and owner destruction may free it while callbacks still run. Reserving capacity merely reduces reallocations; it is not a lifetime or concurrency guarantee. Pinning the Vec object also does not pin its separately allocated element buffer.

Move the data to stable storage, such as a boxed slice that is not resized, owned by a registration object covering every foreign access. Alternatively use an opaque handle whose registry acquires an owning reference for each callback. If the C side retains an Arc-derived raw pointer, specify exactly which registration owns that strong reference and exactly when it is released. Cloning an Arc from an already-freed raw pointer is unsafe.

Define whether callbacks may overlap and which data they mutate. Use a mutex or justified atomics for shared mutation; stable addresses alone do not make access race-free. Document C ABI layout, lengths, null handling, allocator pairing and error translation, preventing unwinding across an incompatible ABI.

Teardown must stop new dispatch, unregister, and wait for all in-flight callbacks to become quiescent before dropping storage/context. Protect the drain barrier against entry racing shutdown. Specify behavior if foreign unregister offers no drain guarantee.

Proposed native tests should force reallocation attempts, callback/drop overlap, repeated registration, cancellation and failure cleanup, using sanitizers/race tools where supported. Passing stress tests cannot prove all memory safety.
answers.verification: Only the supplied ownership scenario was reviewed. Native compilation, sanitizers, concurrency stress and caller-language tests are proposed and were not run.

The checker asserts observable behavior without importing or executing an implementation. Positive cases include both valid boundaries, nearby values and distinct interior ports, so returning one constant or clipping to an incorrect boundary will fail. Equality checks require the port to remain unchanged; result type checks prevent a boolean result from passing merely because True equals 1.

Out-of-range integer cases include zero, negative values, the first value above the maximum and very large magnitudes. They require ValueError. Wrong-type cases require TypeError, covering bool explicitly even though it subclasses int, as well as strings, floats, null and containers. An unexpected exception type propagates and fails the checker rather than being counted as success.

The empty int subclass exercises the stated integer contract: absent a narrower exact-built-in-type rule, a nonboolean int subclass is an integer and must be accepted. Assertions do not demand object identity or incidental exception messages.

A proposed check of this checker would first pass it a known-correct implementation. Only after that should deliberately broken variants be measured: a constant return, unchecked identity, off-by-one lower/upper ranges, bool acceptance and float coercion. Count false rejection of correct behavior separately from caught defects. No implementation or checker was executed here.
answers.verification: Proposed known-correct acceptance followed by six meaningful mutants; all execution remains unperformed.

Use a single PostgreSQL transaction for claim, job, outbox and replay data. Authenticate first and scope a durable idempotency row by a unique (tenant_id, key). Store a canonical payload representation or strong hash with canonicalization versioning, plus the response status/body and job ID. Tenant identity comes from authentication, not an untrusted body field.

Within READ COMMITTED, insert the key row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A concurrent conflicting insert may block on the unique constraint until the first transaction commits or rolls back; it does not necessarily observe a committed “processing” status. The winner creates the job, its outbox event, and the stable replay response in the same transaction, then commits before returning 202 with the job location.

A loser that did not insert reads the committed row in a subsequent statement with fresh visibility. Matching payload replays the stored outcome; changed payload returns 409 without new work. If the first transaction rolls back, its claim/job/outbox all disappear and another requester can become the winner. No separately committed claim, lease or stale-owner takeover is part of this protocol.

A crash before commit leaves no durable command; a lost reply after commit is recovered by replaying the same key. Bound lock/statement waits and return a retryable outcome on timeout. Outbox delivery can repeat, so workers deduplicate by durable job/event identity. Keep key retention aligned with the supported retry window.
answers.verification: Proposed concurrent same-key, changed-payload, cross-tenant, rollback, unknown-commit and duplicate-outbox-delivery tests. No database or endpoint was executed.
